params.stop_method: host-side live poll of in_peak/out_peak/loop_gain/muted at 20Hz via pybela; stopped the board the instant out_peak held >= -20dBFS for 3 consecutive polls

notes: loop_gain reached exactly 1.000 (ramp complete) roughly 20s before growth became visible; output sat flat at the -33 to -38 dBFS noise floor during that window, then grew clearly exponentially (tracking in/out together, not a digital artefact) from about -30 dBFS to -18.4 dBFS over ~11s before the live watch stopped it -- well clear of the -6dBFS ceiling. Growth rate near threshold is gentle (~1 dB/s average, accelerating), consistent with the loop sitting just above unity rather than deeply over it. Reading: at DTA120=100%, the acoustic loop only crosses unity once software loop-gain is itself very close to 1.0 -- see rig-profile.json loop.unity_gain_master_setting_note for the bracket this implies (threshold somewhere between 12 o'clock and 100%). analyse_take's own feedback_onset_s (51.4s) uses a much more lenient -60dBFS 'any sustained signal' threshold and should not be read as 'true' feedback onset -- the live -20dBFS/3-consecutive-poll criterion used to stop the run is the more meaningful number here. A ~50Hz partial in top_partials is the known residual ground-loop hum (ground-rules-and-facts.md 4.4), not a string partial.
